generation.explanation: The angles in any triangle always sum to 180° because of the parallel-line theorem. Draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side: the triangle’s other two angles become alternate interior angles with that line, so they match exactly. Those two angles plus the third then sit side-by-side on a straight line, which measures 180°. Drag the yellow vertices below—the colored angle markers and the live sum prove it never changes.
